original_question: Under Martin's Axiom or weaker hypotheses, construct examples realizing any consistent configuration of Borel-cover properties that is not already covered by the four configurations displayed in Figure 3.
target_in_paper: Section 7, Project 2: "Find constructions, under Martin’s Axiom or weaker hypotheses, for any of the consistent configurations not covered in Figure 3."
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the paper’s target as the Section 7 project about the Borel case: it asks for constructions, it explicitly allows Martin’s Axiom or weaker hypotheses, and it focuses on configurations not already realized by the four examples displayed in Figure 3.
missing_details: The ambient objects are sets of reals X (the paper’s standing convention is to work with spaces homeomorphic to sets of reals unless stated otherwise), not arbitrary spaces by default.
The relevant properties are the Borel-cover properties in the front plane of Figure 2, not Borel-cover properties in general.
To make the question stand-alone, one should specify the reduced Borel diagram’s classes: S1(BΓ,BΓ), S1(BΓ,BΩ), S1(BΓ,B), Sfin(BΩ,BΩ), S1(BΩ,BΓ), S1(BΩ,BΩ), and S1(B,B).
One must define B, BΩ, and BΓ as the families of countable Borel covers, countable Borel ω-covers, and countable Borel γ-covers of X.
The paper uses the Borel-case equivalences S1(BΓ,V) = Sfin(BΓ,V) = Ufin(BΓ,V) for V in {B, BΩ, BΓ}; Figure 2 is already the reduced diagram after these identifications.
"Configuration" should be spelled out as the pattern of which front-plane Borel properties are satisfied by X, consistent with the implication/nonimplication structure encoded by Figure 2.

The surrounding context is the search for uncountable counterexample-type sets of reals in the Borel case under assumptions weaker than CH; without saying this, the problem is less faithful to the paper’s intent.

Figure 3 uses filled bullets to mark exactly which front-plane properties the known examples satisfy; that interpretation is implicit in the draft and should be made explicit in a stand-alone formulation.
refined_question: Let X ⊆ R be an uncountable set of reals, and let B, BΩ, and BΓ denote the families of countable Borel covers, countable Borel ω-covers, and countable Borel γ-covers of X, respectively. In the reduced Borel diagram of Figure 2 (using the Borel equivalences S1(BΓ,V) = Sfin(BΓ,V) = Ufin(BΓ,V) for V ∈ {B, BΩ, BΓ}), can one, under Martin’s Axiom or under hypotheses weaker than Martin’s Axiom, construct for each configuration consistent with that diagram but different from the four already realized in Figure 3(a)–(d), an uncountable set of reals X that realizes exactly that pattern of satisfaction/failure among the front-plane properties S1(BΓ,BΓ), S1(BΓ,BΩ), S1(BΓ,B), Sfin(BΩ,BΩ), S1(BΩ,BΓ), S1(BΩ,BΩ), and S1(B,B)?
justification: The draft is already very close to the paper’s official formulation, and the nearest paper-faithful target is exactly Section 7, Project 2. The necessary sharpening is to unpack what the paper leaves implicit at that point: the standing ambient class of spaces (sets of reals), the meaning of B, BΩ, and BΓ, the fact that Figure 2 is a reduced Borel diagram because of the equivalences proved earlier, and the meaning of a "configuration" as a truth-value pattern on the front plane of that diagram. Section 6.2 shows that the surrounding discussion is about uncountable Borel examples/counterexamples, and Section 7 explains that Figure 3 records the four presently known configurations under hypotheses weaker than Martin’s Axiom.
